messages.author: 6fb9d7eb23edd043
messages.subject: Sampling observed data
parts:
Dear INLA community

I am trying to get samples of the observed data using the posterior found with INLA but I am not sure if I am doing correclty. 
I know about the functions inla.posterior.sample() and inla.posterior.sample.eval(), I am using right now inla.posterior.sample() as I see that in the part "latent" there are the APredictor so if the observed data was of length n, I take the first n predictors, is that correct? And as long as I understand inla.posterior.sample.eval() is only for sampling the posterior predictive.

I see that something similar is done when getting the predictions of the model and the reason why I take the approach mentioned above. As seen in this part of the code we are only taking the index.pred observations when trying to get the predictions:

index.pred <- inla.stack.index(stk.full, "pred")$data
res$summary.fitted.values[index.pred, "mean"] #for the predictions

But if we are trying to get the index of the fitted values it would be:

index.est <- inla.stack.index(stk.full, "est")$data
res$summary.fitted.values[index.est, "mean"] #for the estimations

So if I want to get samples of the fitted values to sample the observed data I do

sim <- inla.posterior.sample(500, res) #In this object in the part of latent I would get the #first n predictors for an observed data of size n, just like for the case of the fitted #values

sim[[1]]$latent[1:n] #where n is the size of the observed data

Is this approach correct to getting samples of the observed data?

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Sampling observed data
parts:
The answer to your final question is “no”, since it produces samples of the predictor values, which are typically the expectation values for the observation model, _not_ ‘observations’ in themselves. Some.g. In a y ~ Poisson(lambda) model, the predictor (with link function applied) gives you lambda values, and to get y values you’d need to call rpois() afterwards. This would make sense for the “pred” part. (And the “est” part, in some cases).
Finn

parts:
Thank you Finn for your answer, I really appreciate it. 
But if that approach is not correct then using your answer I assume then it would be something using rlnorm() as I am using a log normal model. The y~lognormal the predictors would be the mean and the Precision for the lognormal observations that can be obtained from the summary of the model would be sigma, so would be correct to make 

rlnorm(n, first n predictors, precision for the lognormal observations), where n is the size of the observed data

Can this be a correct approach to obtain samples of the observed data?

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Sampling observed data
parts:
Something like that, yes (with precision needing to be converted to the type of parameter required by rlnorm (), etc).
The observed data is what you already have, but it would give you samples of what the model thinks observed data could be like.
Finn

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Sampling observed data

Thank you Finn, everything was really useful. At the end what I did was rnorm(n, n first predictors, 1/sqrt(Precision for the lognormal observations))

I am using rnorm because I want to compared the transformed data, not in the original scale, and I said that in the original scale is lognormal.

I think this works much better. Thank you!!
